QuestionStmt.S: Which of the following is primary allylic alcohol?

Solution.S: An allylic alcohol has the hydroxyl group attached to a carbon atom adjacent to a carbon-carbon double bond. A primary allylic alcohol means the carbon bearing the -OH group is a primary carbon (connected to only one other carbon besides the -OH). Among the options: $\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH_2OH}$ (allyl alcohol) is the correct example. In $\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH(OH)-CH_3}$, the -OH is on a secondary carbon. The other options also have the -OH on primary carbons but the double bond positions differ; however, the simplest and most common primary allylic alcohol is $\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH_2OH}$, which corresponds to option B.
